title: Uncovering the mechanism of female restitution in sugarcane hybrids.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Ran paper_context.py: no PMCID, not open access, no supplement, no accessions in text, no text-mined accessions, no Zenodo/Dryad hits. NCBI elink from PubMed 42557324 returned only related-article links (no GEO, SRA, BioProject). The Nature article page redirects to a login, so the data availability statement could not be read. BioProject search for 'US56-14-4' returned 0 hits; 'LA Purple' returned 30 Saccharum projects, none tied to this paper.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: Everything else comes from the abstract: haplotype-resolved genomes of 2 parents (octoploid S. officinarum LA Purple, decaploid S. spontaneum US56-14-4), 8 F1 hybrids with a 2:1 maternal-to-paternal genome ratio, 2 hybrid assemblies, long-read recombination breakpoint calls, and a new breakpoint-detection algorithm.

a1_downloadable.note: No data repository found: no PMCID, no NCBI links from PubMed, and the paywalled article page blocked the data statement. The likely deposits are raw long reads and assemblies (genome-scale), not tables.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: No prediction target exists. The outputs are genome assemblies and recombination breakpoint calls; any label (say, breakpoint class) would have to be built by re-running the authors' algorithm on raw reads.

a3_inputs_present.note: Inputs would be raw PacBio-type long reads and multi-gigabase polyploid assemblies, not a feature table.

a4_units_stated.note: No tabular measurements were seen, so there are no units to check.

a5_enough_rows.note: The biological units are 8 F1 hybrids and 2 parents. Breakpoint counts were not seen; any table would come from 8 individuals of one cross.

a6_fits_laptop.working_set: unknown; a decaploid/octoploid haplotype-resolved genome plus long reads is likely tens to hundreds of GB
a6_fits_laptop.note: Genome-scale raw data, not a laptop working set.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: No files opened, so nothing could be compared.

a8_label_provenance.note: Breakpoint classes would be the output of the authors' own new algorithm, so learning them would just copy that algorithm.

backbone.name: none applicable (a DNA language model such as AgroNT exists for plant genomes, but there is no labelled task to fit a head to)

integration.partner_dataset: SugarcaneOmics genome browser (NGDC); the 2024 Nature modern-sugarcane R570 genome
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: No ML question that holds up was found; the joins would serve genome comparison, not prediction.

honest_claim_h3: No ML claim is possible: the paper is a mechanistic genomics study of 8 hybrids from one cross, with no label table.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use long-read sequence around chromosome crossover points to predict which kind of crossover pattern each one is.
plain_idea.train_on: Long-read sequencing reads covering recombination breakpoints (crossover points) in 8 sugarcane hybrids; number of breakpoints unknown.
plain_idea.predict: Breakpoint class (the two classes the paper describes), which comes from the authors' own detection algorithm, not from a separate measurement.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: It would mostly copy the authors' algorithm on one cross. Breeders gain more from the genomes directly than from a model.

label_elsewhere.sources: None known. Breakpoint-class calls for second division restitution (where the egg cell skips its second halving division) appear to exist only in this paper; not searched beyond one web search.
label_elsewhere.why: There is no outside labelled data to train or validate on.

ml_idea: None that survives. A breakpoint-class classifier would learn the authors' algorithm's output from 8 hybrids of a single cross, from raw long-read data.

effort.compute_note: Not estimated: no data files were located and the project fails Part A.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Read the data availability statement for a processed breakpoint table. Without one, the project is dead.

verdict_reason: A paywalled genome-assembly paper with no data repository found, no label column (breakpoint classes come from the authors' own algorithm, which fails A8), only 8 hybrids from one cross (fails A5), and raw data at genome scale (fails A6).
